bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists in decompress_fuzzer where header sizes are not properly validated, potentially leading to errors detected by address sanitizer (asan).
bug_description.normalized: The staged 3569-byte witness is a malformed Blosc buffer processed by `tests/fuzz/fuzz_decompress.c`. The harness only checks `size >= BLOSC_MIN_HEADER_LENGTH`, `cbytes == size`, and `nbytes != 0` after `blosc_cbuffer_sizes()`, then allocates `cbytes` bytes and calls `blosc_decompress()` without the later-added `blosc_cbuffer_validate(data, size, &nbytes)` guard. In the witness header, bytes 4-7 are `00 09 05 ff`; `blosc_cbuffer_sizes()` first obtains signed `int32_t -16447232` from `sw32_(_src + 4)` and then casts that result to a nonzero `size_t nbytes`, so the nonzero check passes, while bytes 12-15 decode to `cbytes = 3569`, matching the file size. `initialize_context_decompression()` re-reads the same 4 bytes as signed `int32_t sourcesize = -16447232`, reads `blocksize = 1535`, and computes `nblocks = -10714`. Because the header flags byte is `0x5f`, the decompressor takes the extended-header branch, sets `bstarts = src + 32`, and because byte `src[0x1f]` is `0xff`, it enters the dictionary path. The statement `sw32_(context->bstarts + context->nblocks)` therefore dereferences `src - 42824`, producing the witnessed `MemorySanitizer: SEGV` READ in `blosc-private.h:51`.

source.description: First project statement that consumes the staged buffer and materializes the attacker-controlled `nbytes` header field into harness-visible state.
source.value_from: In `gt_results/arvo_23717/poc`, header bytes 4-7 are `00 09 05 ff`. `sw32_(_src + 4)` returns signed `int32_t -16447232` from those bytes, and `blosc_cbuffer_sizes()` immediately casts that result to a nonzero `size_t nbytes` before the harness applies its shallow `nbytes != 0` check.

tainted_value_origin.description: The same header bytes from step 1 are re-read as signed `int32_t sourcesize = -16447232`, which is the direct value later divided by `blocksize` to derive the negative `nblocks` used in the crashing pointer arithmetic.

root_cause.description: The harness enters `blosc_decompress()` after only the shallow `cbytes == size` and `nbytes != 0` checks. It never performs the full header validation that the fix patch adds immediately before this call.
root_cause.note: The staged patch inserts `if (blosc_cbuffer_validate(data, size, &nbytes) != 0) return 0;` between the shallow header checks and this decompression call.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer crash site. `sw32_()` dereferences the pointer derived from `context->bstarts + context->nblocks`, which in the reproduced run points 42824 bytes before the staged input buffer.
sink.note: The saved trace reports `MemorySanitizer: SEGV` caused by a READ at `blosc/blosc-private.h:51:15` in `sw32_`, with the caller frame at `initialize_context_decompression` line 1477.

parser_admitted.description: After the staged buffer passes the harness's shallow `size`, `cbytes`, and nonzero `nbytes` checks and `malloc(3569)` succeeds, the harness hands the witness to `blosc_decompress()`, entering the vulnerable decompression parser.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness parses the staged header with `blosc_cbuffer_sizes()`, accepts the buffer because `cbytes == size` and the signed header value is cast to a nonzero `size_t nbytes`, and calls `blosc_decompress()` without the later-added full-header validator.
The decompressor re-reads the same header as signed values, turns the forged `sourcesize` into `nblocks = -10714`, and takes the extended-header dictionary path based on the witness flag bytes.
Dictionary setup indexes `bstarts + nblocks`, producing a pointer 42824 bytes before the input buffer; `sw32_()` dereferences it and MemorySanitizer reports the saved SEGV READ.

fine_trace.note: Source. `blosc_cbuffer_sizes()` reads header bytes 4-7 `00 09 05 ff`, `sw32_(_src + 4)` yields signed `int32_t -16447232`, and the assignment casts that result to `size_t nbytes`. This is the first project-side materialization of the malformed size field, and the later harness guard only observes that the casted `nbytes` is nonzero.
Reads header bytes 12-15 `f1 0d 00 00` as `cbytes = 3569`, exactly the staged file size. The harness uses this value both for its size equality check and as the eventual decompressor `destsize`.
Present guard. In the reproduced witness `cbytes == size == 3569`, so the harness does not reject the buffer on compressed-length mismatch.
Present guard. Because step 1 stored a nonzero `size_t` in `nbytes`, this predicate is false and the malformed header survives the harness's only `nbytes` check.

Root cause. The harness uses `cbytes = 3569` as both the output allocation size and decompressor `destsize`, and because `malloc` succeeded in the reproduced run it calls `blosc_decompress()` without any full-header validation. The staged patch adds `blosc_cbuffer_validate(data, size, &nbytes)` immediately before this use.
The decompressor re-reads the same header bytes from step 1 as signed `int32_t` and stores `sourcesize = -16447232`. This signed form is the value that later drives negative block-count arithmetic.

Re-reads header bytes 8-11 `ff 05 00 00` as `blocksize = 1535`. With `destsize = 3569` from step 5 and `typesize = 4`, the existing `blocksize/typesize` guard at lines 1442-1444 does not reject this buffer.
Derives the block count from the signed header values. In C this yields `nblocks = -10714` and `leftover = -1242`, so the `leftover > 0` adjustment is skipped and `nblocks` stays negative.

The witness flag byte is `0x5f`, so both `BLOSC_DOSHUFFLE` and `BLOSC_DOBITSHUFFLE` are set. The decompressor therefore takes the extended-header branch, materializes `blosc2_flags = src + 0x1f`, and sets `bstarts = src + 32`.
Byte `src[0x1f]` in the staged witness is `0xff`, so the `BLOSC2_USEDICT` bit is set and the dictionary-handling path executes.
Unsafe pointer arithmetic. With `bstarts = src + 32` and `nblocks = -10714`, the argument to `sw32_()` becomes `src - 42824`, i.e. 42824 bytes before the start of the staged input buffer.
Sink. `sw32_()` dereferences `pa_[0..3]` from the out-of-bounds pointer computed in step 11; the saved MemorySanitizer trace reports the SEGV at line 51 while reading `pa_[3]`.

poc.trigger: The staged witness is the 3569-byte file `gt_results/arvo_23717/poc`. Its header satisfies the harness's shallow acceptance checks (`size >= 16`, `cbytes == size`, and `nbytes` becomes a nonzero `size_t` after the signed `sw32_()` read) and then drives `initialize_context_decompression()` into the extended-header dictionary path, where `sw32_(context->bstarts + context->nblocks)` reads before the input buffer and MemorySanitizer reports the saved SEGV.

format.name: Blosc compressed buffer
format.contract: A 3569-byte input whose Blosc header bytes are: version `0x02`, flags `0x5f`, typesize `0x04`, `nbytes` field `00 09 05 ff`, `blocksize` field `ff 05 00 00`, `cbytes` field `f1 0d 00 00` (so `cbytes == 3569 == file size`), and byte `src[0x1f] = 0xff`. Under the vulnerable harness, those exact fields make `blosc_cbuffer_sizes()` accept the buffer, make `initialize_context_decompression()` compute `sourcesize = -16447232` and `nblocks = -10714`, and cause the dictionary-size read `sw32_(bstarts + nblocks)` to dereference `src - 42824`.
